text: Agile methodology is a popular approach to project management, especially in software development. Instead of working on a huge project all at once, teams break the work into small, manageable pieces called sprints, which typically last two to four weeks. Before each sprint, the team reviews its backlog, a prioritized list of tasks and features. These tasks are often written as user stories, short descriptions from a user’s perspective, such as “As a customer, I want to track my order so I can see when it arrives.” Every day, the team holds a quick standup meeting to share progress and address challenges. This iterative process allows for continuous feedback and adjustments, ensuring the final product closely matches what users actually need.
